plan_review.notes: Adversarial-style rubber-duck review of the stateless, marker-based, review-gated design. 4 blocking concerns: (1) no auto-trigger on review-issue close -> added issues:[closed,reopened] trigger + concurrency group; (2) any closed state treated as approval -> gated on state_reason==completed vs not_planned rejection; (3) no pin to reviewed file revision -> added epicContentHash + reviewHashMarker drift detection; (4) no concurrency control -> added concurrency group (group: epic-create). 3 non-blocking concerns addressed: node.id charset validation, description/review field type validation, duplicate epic_id across a multi-file batch (assertUniqueEpicIds). One non-blocking suggestion (CODEOWNERS entry for docs/knowledge/epics/**) consciously deferred as a separate governance change out of this tasks scope; noted in the PR/handoff. All fixes were refinements to the same core design (stateless marker-based issues, no control-plane file) rather than a different architecture, so plan_divergence=minor.

rounds.notes: Shell injection via workflow_dispatch epic_path interpolated into run: blocks; state_reason:null on a closed issue treated as approval; a stale not_planned rejection permanently blocking a revised (different-hash) plan.

Diagnostic promised a fresh review issue could be filed for a revised plan but no mechanism existed to create one; left unresolved at the two-round cap and escalated to the maintainer instead of continuing the automated loop.

escalated_to_human.reason: The second automated review round still had a validated unresolved concern, so the review loop hit the two-round cap and was escalated instead of continuing rounds 3-5.

code_review.human_disposition: Maintainer dispatched CI recovery on 2026-08-24 for the exact review-thread blockers. The follow-up recovery commit addresses the applicable findings rather than treating the over-cap clean rounds as policy evidence.

findings.detail: The graded diff includes an unrelated Floor 3 starter-Companion feature and associated engine, map-generation, headless-runner, and test changes, despite the stated task being only the .epic.json-to-GitHub-issues workflow. Split the unrelated Floor 3 changes into their own reviewable change set.

independent_grade.notes: The epic workflow implementation and its focused tests are substantially complete, but the diff is not scoped to the declared task: it bundles a separate gameplay feature and its supporting changes. This warrants human review under the grading rules.
